title: Smördegsstänger med Ost (Puff Pastry Sticks with Cheese)
description: A pastry dish made with grated cheese, egg yolk, and flour.
steps: Prepare the puff pastry as in recipe no. 33.
The last time it is rolled out, sprinkle a little of the grated cheese on the rolled-out dough and repeat this until the dough is fully rolled out, then let it rest 1 hour.
Roll it out to an oblong strip of 1 cm. thickness, which is cut out into 8 cm. long sticks.
Twist them 2 turns or leave them straight, brush with egg yolk, place on a well-cleaned baking sheet and bake to a golden-brown color in a warm oven.
Serve with consommé or clear broth.

title: Smörgåspudding (Bread and Butter Pudding)
description: A pudding made with bread, butter, and apple or fruit.

ingredients.name: apple compote or other fruit
ingredients.sourceText: 2 cups apple compote or other fruit

steps: Cut the bread into slices, and spread butter on one side.
Whisk the milk and egg together, and dip the bread lightly in it.

Grease a form with washed butter and sprinkle it with finely crushed rusks; on the bottom of the form place a layer of the sandwiches, also around the edges of the form — then a layer of apple compote or other fruit.
Continue until the form is filled; the top layer should be sandwiches.
Whisk the eggs and milk together and pour over the pudding, place it in gentle oven heat.
When it has taken on a nice, golden-brown color, it is ready.
Serve either in its form, or turn it out after most of the heat has subsided.

title: Smörkäx (Butter Cookies)
description: A biscuit made with butter, wheat flour, and milk.
steps: Sift the flour. Work the butter into half of the flour with fingertips, then add the milk and finally the rest of the flour except 1 kkp, which is set aside for baking.
Work the dough until it becomes even and smooth, then cover it and let it stand in a cold place for one day.
Roll out the dough thinly, prick it well and cut out with a large round mould into cookies, which are baked light yellow in a warm oven.
Serve with marmalade or butter.

title: Smörsås (Butter Sauce)
description: A sauce made with butter, egg yolks, and cream.

ingredients.name: 4 deciliters boiling water with 3 gr. salt
ingredients.sourceText: 4 deciliters boiling water with 3 gr. salt

steps: Fry the butter and flour for 5 minutes without browning.
Add the water gradually, but the sauce should not boil.
Add the egg yolks whipped with the cream and let the sauce simmer.
Season with the lemon juice, strain through cloth, and stir in the melted butter.
Serve with fish, meat, and vegetables.
The sauce can also be cooked on fish stock and cream, and in the simplest case on good milk.
Shrimp sauce is prepared in the same way.

title: Smörtårta (Butter Cake)
description: A cake made with butter, apple, and cream.

ingredients.name: 5 hg. fine butter (equal weight with the dough)
ingredients.sourceText: 5 hg. fine butter (equal weight with the dough)

ingredients.name: 30 gr. finely chopped, roasted sweet almonds
ingredients.sourceText: 30 gr. finely chopped, roasted sweet almonds

steps: Prepare the butter dough as in recipe no. 33 and roll out to 2 bottoms, one 2 cm., the other 3 cm. thick.
From the bowl or dish on which the cake is to be served, take a measurement. This is easiest done by cutting a pattern of paper, after which the dough is cut out with a pastry cutter.
The dough shrinks during baking and should therefore be 4 cm. wider in circumference than the pattern.
Place the thinnest bottom on a baking sheet and brush with egg white, but none of this must come down over the edge, as it prevents the butter dough from rising.
Cut the other bottom into a 3 cm. wide ring, which is placed on top of the bottom and carefully brushed with egg white.
Bake the cake in a hot oven and turn it often, so that it becomes evenly baked and gets a beautiful golden-brown color.
Roll out the remaining dough to 2 cm. thickness and cut with a cutter into strips, which are laid in diagonal squares, so that they form a lattice that fits inside the ring on the cake.
Brush the lattice and bake as before.
Fill the cake with apple compote or apple purée, spread the cream whipped to stiff peaks over it, and sprinkle with the roasted almonds.
Place the lattice on top and serve the cake at once.

title: Smörtårtor (Butter Tarts)
description: A pastry dish made with butter, wheat flour, and egg yolks.
steps: Prepare the butter dough as fine butter dough (no. 548)
Roll out to 1/2 cm thickness and cut into round cakes
Place a little apple sauce on one half of the cake and fold the other half over, pressing the edges well together
Cut the edge with a piping tool or knife into round points

Alternatively, cut out square cakes and make an incision in each corner with a piping tool, place a little apple sauce in the middle, fold every other of the eight flaps up over the apple sauce, and press them together against each other
Bake the pastries in a warm oven

title: Snöpudding (Snow Pudding)
description: A pudding made with cream, vanilla pod, and egg yolks.
steps: The thin cream, sugar and vanilla are brought to a boil until the cream has acquired vanilla flavor.
The egg yolks are added one at a time while whisking vigorously, and the cream is allowed to simmer over the heat until it thickens.
The pan is then lifted off the heat, and whisking is continued until the cream is completely cold.
The thick cream is then whisked to stiff peaks and folded into the cream.
This is poured into a freezing mold and frozen until half frozen, then packed alternately with the crushed biscuits or fruit in a water-rinsed mold with a tight lid.
The mold is placed in crushed ice and salt.
The ice and salt should lie under, around and over the mold for 2-3 hours.
The pudding is turned out and garnished with biscuits or fruit.

title: Sockerstruvor (Sugar Pastries, 25-28 pieces)
description: A pastry dish made with sugar, egg yolk, and egg whites.
steps: Beat the egg yolk and four of the egg whites with the sugar until white and fluffy.
Sift the flour and carefully fold it into the batter.
Lastly, fold in the remaining egg whites beaten to stiff peaks.
Heat the deep fat in a pot, no more than a small teacup full.
Through a pastry horn or ordinary funnel, drizzle a tablespoon of the batter back and forth into the fat so that it forms a latticed cake.
When the pastry is golden brown on the underside, turn it with a slotted spoon, and when it has achieved an even, beautiful color, remove it, bend it over a stick, and let it drain on gray paper.
Sprinkle the pastries with sugar before serving.

title: Sofiatårta (Sofia Cake)
description: A cake made with sweet almonds, bitter almonds, and semolina.

ingredients.name: washed butter for the pan

ingredients.name: crushed rusks for the pan

steps: Beat the egg yolks with the sugar for 1/2 hour.
During beating, add water twice, 1 tablespoon each time.
Blanch the almonds, dry them well in the oven, and grate or press through an almond mill and blend with the semolina.
Stir the dry mixture into the egg batter, and last fold in the egg whites beaten to stiff peaks.
Pour the batter into a buttered and rusk-strewn form or pan and bake for 1 hour in moderate oven heat.
This cake is particularly good with coffee and can, if desired, be glazed with chocolate glaze, or garnished like an ordinary cake.

title: Soppa på Blåbär (Bilberry Soup)
description: A soup made with bilberries, lemon, and potato flour.

ingredients.name: fresh bilberries or 4 deciliters dried bilberries
ingredients.sourceText: 1 liter fresh bilberries or 4 deciliters dried bilberries

steps: Clean the berries and rinse them in a colander, then let them drain.
Place them in boiling water with the lemon peel and cinnamon and let cook until they are loose.
Strain the berries from the liquid, add the sugar to the juice, bring to a boil, and thicken with the potato flour mixed with 1/2 tablespoon cold water.
Let cook for 2 minutes, season to taste, and set aside to cool.
Serve with dumplings, whipped cream, and rusks or biscuits.
If using dried bilberries, rinse them thoroughly in lukewarm water and let them soak overnight in the water in which they will be cooked.

title: Soppa på blåkål (Red Cabbage Soup)
description: A soup made with cabbage, broth or pork, and white pepper.
steps: Put the cabbage (which should be frozen) in water so that the ice is drawn out.
Grate it thereafter, rinse it well and blanch it 1/2 hour in salted water.
Lay the cabbage on a sieve to drain and chop it thereafter with flour until it becomes very fine.
Melt the butter in a pan, add the cabbage and let it fry with frequent stirring.
Add the boiling broth, and let the soup cook 1/2 hour.
Season it thereafter and serve with meatballs or pork sausage.
The thickest cabbage stems can be blanched, peeled, cut into slices, dipped in egg and breadcrumbs and fried golden brown in butter and served in the cabbage.

title: Soppa på färska gurkor (Fresh Cucumber Soup)

ingredients.sourceText: 1 msk. strong meat gravy or meat extract

Add the broth, bring the soup to a good boil and season it.
Finally stir in the cold butter, and serve the soup.

title: Soppa på murklor (Mushroom Soup)
description: A soup made with mushrooms, broth, and bread.

ingredients.name: 1 lit. fresh or 1/2 lit. canned porcini mushrooms
ingredients.sourceText: 1 lit. fresh or 1/2 lit. canned porcini mushrooms

steps: Clean and rinse the mushrooms very well (if they have not been canned, in which case the broth is important for the fine taste of the soup).
Fry half of the mushrooms in 1 msk. of the butter and then let them cook together with the raw mushrooms in the broth, and add the salt.
When the mushrooms are tender, strain them out.
Cut the wheat bread into approximately 2 cm. cubes, which are fried in the rest of the butter.
Add the fried bread to the soup, which should cook a further 15 minutes, then season with a very little cayenne pepper.
Whisk the egg yolks in a soup bowl, and pour the soup in while whisking.

title: Soppa på torra plommon (Dried Plum Soup)
description: A soup made with prunes or plums, lemon, and potato flour.
steps: Rinse the plums very well in lukewarm water and let them drain.
Pound half of them in a mortar so that the pits are crushed.
Set the pounded and whole plums on to boil in cold water and let them cook until they are completely soft, then strain them.

Bring the strained soup to boil together with the sugar and thicken it with the potato flour, stirred in 1/2 kkp cold water.
Let it cook 2 minutes thereafter, season it, and serve preferably cold with whipped cream and small rusks or biscuits.

title: Soppa på villebråd eller fågel (Game or Poultry Soup)
description: A soup made with bones or hare, carrots, and celeriac.

ingredients.name: Remnants and bones of hare or scraps and remnants of poultry
ingredients.sourceText: Remnants and bones of hare or scraps and remnants of poultry

steps: If raw bones and scraps are used, the soup will be finer in taste.
Cut away the best meat and use it for forcemeat or meatballs, which are served in the soup.
Cut the remnants and bones into small pieces and brown in 2 tablespoons of the butter together with the cleaned and cut vegetables and parsley.
Add the cold broth, place in the whole spices and let the soup cook with a tightly closed lid about 2 hours.
Separate all meat well from the bones, which should cook further in the broth for 1/2 hour.
Grind the meat 4 times through a meat grinder, mix with 1 deciliter broth and pass through a sieve.
Strain and skim the broth and measure it—should be 1.5 liters.
Fry the remaining butter with the flour for 2 minutes, add the broth and the passed meat and let the soup cook for 5 minutes.
Season with the spices, wine and butter and serve with meatballs of game or cheese croutons.

title: Soppa à la Hedin (Hedin's Soup)
description: A soup made with veal, broth, and lemon juice.
steps: The veal sweetbread should soak in water for 1 hour to draw out the blood, then blanch it (place in cold, lightly salted water and let it cook 10 minutes) and cool in cold water.

Heat the broth with the parsley, add the sweetbread and let it cook until it is white and firm, about 45 minutes. Remove it, let it cool and cut into fine dice, which are placed in the soup bowl. Strain the broth.

Fry butter and flour for 2 minutes, add the broth little by little and let it cook with stirring for 5 minutes. Season the soup with lemon juice, wine and spices. Beat the egg yolks and whisk them into the soup, which is then poured over the sweetbread in the soup bowl.

title: Spansk Sås (Spanish Sauce)
description: A sauce made with stock, onion, and carrot.
steps: Put the stock on with the onion, parsley and carrot and let it cook until it has a good, strong flavor.
Strain it and skim carefully.
Fry together the butter and flour, add the stock, and let the sauce come to a good boil.
Move it then to low heat to simmer for 1.5 hours.
Now add the meat stock according to the roast to which the sauce is to be served, and let the sauce come to another boil, then taste and serve.

title: Sparrissoufflé (Asparagus Soufflé)
description: Prepared with asparagus, white pepper, and breadcrumbs.

ingredients.name: 3 hg fresh asparagus or 1 can omelet asparagus (1/2 liter)
ingredients.sourceText: 3 hg fresh asparagus or 1 can omelet asparagus (1/2 liter)

ingredients.name: butter (10 gr) for the mold
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 tbsp butter (10 gr) for the mold

steps: Scrape the asparagus, rinse, cut into three pieces and cook until tender in 4 dcl water with 1/{{source-6}}.
If using canned asparagus, cut it in half and place on a sieve to drain.
Fry the butter and flour together for 2 minutes.
Add the hot asparagus broth and milk and let the sauce boil for 5 minutes.
Pour into a bowl; when cooled, add the egg yolks one at a time and stir the mixture for 10 minutes.
Mix in the well-drained asparagus along with the seasonings and the egg whites beaten until stiff peaks form.
Taste and adjust seasonings.
Pour into a buttered and breadcrumb-lined mold and bake in regular oven heat for about 45 minutes.
If using a metal form, bake in a water bath in the oven for about 1 hour and turn out.
Serve immediately upon removal from the oven as a middle course with hollandaise or stirred butter.

title: Spicken Sill (Pickled Herring for 6 persons)
description: Prepared with fat and white pepper.
steps: Let the herring soak in water for 12 hours, changing the water once.
Fillet, clean, rinse and dry with a fish towel.
Rub with pepper and let rest 1 hour.
Dry again thoroughly, cut into 1 1/2 cm. wide pieces crosswise, arrange on a platter and garnish with parsley or dill.
Serve with fresh or braised potatoes or braised green peas as a breakfast or dinner course.

title: Sponge-cakes (Sponge Cakes)
description: A cake made with wheat flour, lemon or almond, and eggs.

ingredients.name: wheat flour equal to the weight of 3 small eggs (= 180 gr.)
ingredients.sourceText: wheat flour equal to the weight of 3 small eggs (= 180 gr.)

ingredients.name: granulated sugar equal to the weight of 4 eggs (= 240 gr.)
ingredients.sourceText: granulated sugar equal to the weight of 4 eggs (= 240 gr.)

ingredients.name: grated zest of 1 lemon or 3 drops almond essence
ingredients.sourceText: grated zest of 1 lemon or 3 drops almond essence

ingredients.name: washed butter for the molds
ingredients.sourceText: 2 tbsp. washed butter for the molds

steps: Fine wheat flour is dried and sifted.
The egg yolks are stirred with the sugar until the mixture becomes white.
The flour is added together with the lightly grated lemon zest or almond essence.
The egg whites are beaten to stiff peaks and carefully folded into the batter.
Sponge-cake molds or regular smooth pastry molds are greased with washed butter, sprinkled with sugar and filled to three-quarters with batter.
The cakes are placed in a fairly warm oven to bake through and get a beautiful golden color.
They are turned out of the molds while still warm, sugared over and allowed to cool.

title: Spritsad Potatis (Piped Potatoes)
description: Prepared with potatoes, cream, and eggs.
steps: Peel the potatoes raw, cook them and mash them with a fork or press them through a potato ricer.
Whisk the egg yolks with the cream and stir into the mash together with the seasonings and the cold butter.
Then press the purée through a piping bag with a coarse star tip onto the serving dish.
Piped potatoes are used mainly as a garnish for meat dishes, such as larded ox hare, cutlets etc.
The potato mash can also be piped out into an omelette pan, sprinkled with finely crushed rusks and put in the oven to get a nice brown color. It is then served with the smorgasbord.

title: Spunnet Socker (Spun Sugar)
description: Prepared with powdered sugar and water.
steps: Cook caramel sugar to 180° from the powdered sugar, water, and glucose.
Cool rapidly by dipping the pan briefly in cold water.
Place the pan tilted in a frame of straw.
Lightly oil a marble slab or 2-3 baking sheets.
Oil a narrow stick and place it on the slab under a weight so it stands away from the slab.
With a broken whisk or broad fork, fling the sugar right and left over the stick until you have the needed amount.
Cut the threads with a heated knife and immediately wrap them around the dish to be garnished.
The sugar can be colored with various caramel colors.

description: Prepared with sugar, water, and oil.
steps: Cook rock sugar, water, and glucose to caramel sugar (180°). Cool rapidly by dipping the pan briefly in cold water, then place tilted in a ring of straw.
Lightly oil a marble slab or 2-3 baking sheets. Oil a thin stick and place it on the slab under a weight (such as a heavy weight) so it stands above the slab.
Using a broken whisk or broad fork, fling the sugar back and forth over the stick until you have the desired amount.
Cut the threads with a heated knife and immediately wrap around the dish to be garnished. The sugar can be colored with various caramel colors.

title: Späckad kalvsadel (Larded Veal Saddle)
description: Prepared with veal, fat, and broth or water.
steps: Wash the veal saddle with a cloth dipped in hot water and lard with fine larding fat strips turned in salt.
Grease a hot roasting pan with 1 tablespoon of butter and place the saddle in it.
Melt the remaining butter and pour it hot over the saddle.
Put the roast in the oven, brown it, add the hot broth or water, and baste with its drippings every ten minutes.
Roasting takes approximately 1 1/2 hours.
Strain and skim the meat stock, and prepare the sauce according to general sauce rules.

title: Späckad oxhare (Larded Beef Hare)
description: Prepared with beef, lard, and broth or water.
steps: Wash the meat with a cloth dipped in hot water and lard it thereafter in dense rows with finely cut lard strips.
Heat the butter in a roasting pan, and brown the meat in it, salt it and dilute with half of the boiling broth.
Let the hare thereafter slowly roast with a tightly closed lid for 2 hours, during which it is occasionally diluted and basted with the broth.
Slice it into thin slices, lay it together again and place on the serving platter and garnish with vegetables.
Strain and skim the beef stock, and prepare the sauce according to general rules for sauces.

title: Späckad Oxhare (Larded Beef Hare)
description: Prepared with beef, lard, and white pepper.
steps: The hare, which should have hung 4-8 days depending on the season, is prepared and larded (see page 232), rubbed with spices and tied so that it has a beautiful shape.

The butter is browned in an iron pot, the meat is placed in it and browned beautifully on all sides, diluted with half of the broth and put in a hot oven to roast about 3/4-1 hour, basting it every 10th minute and diluting as needed.

Sliced into thin slices, placed on a hot platter, moistened with a couple of tablespoons of sauce, garnished with parsley and vegetables or vegetable salad in shells and served with strained sauce, see no. 429. The hare can also be diluted with cream instead of broth, served then with browned potatoes and currant jelly.

title: Späckad svlnkarré (Larded Pork Loin)
description: Prepared with lemon, white pepper, and prunes.
steps: Carefully trim most of the fat from the loin and loosen the bone halfway with a pointed knife.
Dry it with a cloth wrung out in hot water, beat lightly with a damp mallet, and rub well with lemon.
Rub the loin with a mixture of salt, white pepper, and ginger.
Rinse the prunes well in lukewarm water, blanch 3 minutes in 3 dcl. water, and save the liquid for the gravy.

title: Stekt and (Roasted Duck)
description: Prepared with ducks, broth, and lemon juice.
steps: Pluck the ducks, singe, remove innards, rinse very well and dry and truss them. Rub them in with the liver until they have taken on a reddish-brown color, then brown them in the butter and salt them. Pour the boiling broth in little by little, and let the ducks roast about 1 hour, while they are frequently basted with their stock. Serve the ducks very hot.
Strain and skim the sauce, season it with lemon juice and soy sauce and serve as stock. If desired thickened, prepare it according to general rules for sauces.

title: Stekt benfri abborre (Fried Boneless Perch)
description: Prepared with perch, vinegar, and fish stock.
steps: Scale, clean, rinse, and dry the fish thoroughly.
Cut it open along the back and remove the backbone along with all small bones.
Rub the fillets with vinegar and salt and dredge them in the finely crushed hardtack.
Butter a long pan with half of the butter and lay the perch in it; place the remaining butter in flakes on top of the fish.
Set it in the oven, and when it is browned, add the fish stock (made from the head, skin, and bones), and allow the perch to cook for approximately 20 minutes.
Whisk the pan with cream and pour the sauce over the fish.

title: Stekt fasan (Roasted Pheasant)
description: Prepared with pheasants, lard, and sauce.

ingredients.name: For sauce: the butter in which the birds were browned
ingredients.sourceText: For sauce: the butter in which the birds were browned

steps: The cock pheasant's meat is considered finer than hen and is therefore preferred for roasting. The plumage is magnificent and used by many for decoration. The bird should hang for a few days before preparation so that the meat becomes juicy and obtains the fine flavor of game which is lacking in the freshly slaughtered bird. When it is to be cleaned, first save the head with the neck, wings and tail. The bird is then plucked and treated as stated in the introduction to poultry, larded on the breast and legs with finely cut strips of lard and tied. The birds are then browned in the butter together with the giblets in a roasting pan which must not be so large that they do not just fit. When the birds are well browned, they are removed together with the giblets. The butter in the pan is fried with the flour for 2 minutes, the broth and cream are added and the sauce is allowed to boil for 5 minutes, after which it is seasoned with the spices. The birds are placed in with the breast up and allowed to roast slowly until tender, or 1 to 1 1/2 hours.

Rinse the prunes well in lukewarm water, let them lie for 10 minutes in hot water, wrap them in a cloth and pit them.
Cut the hare open lengthwise, fill it with the apples and prunes and sew it together.
Brown the butter in a roasting pan, lay the hare in with the meat side down and brown it well on all sides.
Dilute first with hot prune stock and thereafter with water, mixed with meat extract and salt.
Let the hare roast slowly with the lid tightly closed until tender, approximately 1 3/4 hours, basting it over approximately every 10 minutes.
Serve with fried potatoes and peas.

title: Stekt färsk skinka (Roasted Fresh Ham)
description: Prepared with ham, white pepper, and lard.

ingredients.name: good meat stock or broth
ingredients.sourceText: 3/4 liter good meat stock or broth

steps: Dry the ham with a cloth wrung out in hot water, and score the skin 1 cm deep in diagonal squares.
Rub the underside and in the scores with a mixture of salt and pepper.
Spread the lard slices in a baking pan, place the ham on top with skin side up.
Set in a hot oven and roast until tender, or approximately 2 1/2 hours.
When the skin pieces get a nice yellow color, harden, and come loose, remove them and use for garnish.
After the ham has roasted approximately 1 1/2 hours, dilute it with the boiling meat stock, added with the parsley and bay leaf.

title: Stekt fårsadel (Roasted Lamb Saddle)
description: Prepared with lamb, lard, and broth or water.
steps: The lamb saddle, which should have hung 8-14 days, is beaten well, then washed with a cloth dipped in hot water.
Remove the fat on the back and kidneys and some of the ribs so the thin sides can be folded up.
Cut the lard into fine strips, roll in salt, and lard the saddle with them.
Bind it and place on a long pan brushed with butter, put in the oven and roast at good heat for 2-3 hours.
Add broth and often baste with its drippings. If the roast becomes too brown, cover with buttered paper at the end of roasting.
Place on a platter and garnish with potato croquettes, glazed carrots, and green beans.
Strain the sauce, skim, and serve as gravy.

title: Stekt gås (Roasted Goose)
description: Prepared with goose, lemon, and prunes.

ingredients.name: fresh or 3 hectograms dried apples
ingredients.sourceText: 2 liters fresh or 3 hectograms dried apples

steps: Open and clean the goose, rinse well and dry with a cloth. Rub inside and outside with the lemon; sprinkle a little salt inside.
Rinse the fruit (remove blossom ends) and fill the goose with it, then sew it shut neatly and fasten the legs well along the sides.

Place on a long pan and put in a hot oven to brown slowly under frequent basting with the fat that forms. When well browned, sprinkle with the remaining salt, add the boiling liquid and roast for 3-4 hours, basting every ten minutes.
Cut the goose and place it whole again on the serving platter, garnished with the apples and prunes.
Strain the sauce, skim it and serve as gravy. It can also be thickened like a regular sauce if desired.

Prepare the sauce according to the general rules for sauces and pour it over the liver.

title: Stekt hare (Roasted Hare)
description: Prepared with hare, lemon, and lard.
steps: The hare should have hung a few days to become tender. Skin it, and remove all membranes very carefully. Cut the head off at the shoulders, as well as the thin parts on the sides. Break the back into 5–6 connected pieces, likewise break the hind legs. Tuck one hind leg between the tendons in the other. Rinse the hare well, dry with a cloth and rub with the lemon until the meat has a fresh and sour smell. Lard it thereafter with the lard cut into fine strips in four rows on each side of the back and on the meatiest part of the leg. Heat the butter in a roasting pan, brown the hare therein on all sides, salt and dilute with broth little by little. Let it then roast until done with a tightly closed lid, for which 1–1½ hours are required.
The hare can either be served with its stock, or the sauce can be thickened according to general rules for sauces.

title: Stekt Hare (Roasted Hare)
description: Prepared with hare, lard, and white pepper.
steps: Hares should not weigh more than stated above, as much larger ones are usually old, coarse and tough in meat. The hare should hang for 3-6 days, depending on the season, to become tender. Skin it (see roe deer, no. 584), remove the head, hind legs and shoulders, then lay the hare on its back and cut off the ribs down to the fillets. Rinse it very thoroughly and dry it, then loosen all membranes with a sharp knife and remove them without damaging the meat. If desired, place the hare in milk afterwards and let it stand until the next day, when it is taken out and wrapped well in cloth. Break the backbone and hind legs on the inside to facilitate carving. Lard the hare on the back, hind legs and shoulders with fine strips of lard dipped in a mixture of salt and white pepper. Brown the butter in a roasting pot, place the back, hind legs and shoulders with the meaty sides down, brown beautifully on both sides, then add first the boiling broth, then the cream. Let it braise slowly with a tightly closed lid until tender, or about 1 1/2 hours. Cut the hare into attractive pieces, arrange on a hot platter, garnish with browned potatoes, salad or parsley, serve with strained sauce (see no. 429) mixed with 1 tablespoon lingonberry jelly, and with green salad and acidic salads.

title: Stekt Helgeflundra (Fried Halibut)
description: Prepared with halibut, lemon, and salt.
steps: Clean the fish piece, remove the dark skin and treat the fish thereafter as in the previous recipe
Once the fish piece has been rubbed with lemon, brush it with the beaten egg on the side from which the skin has been removed, and sprinkle with crushed hardtack

Butter a long pan with half of the butter over a space as large as the fish piece occupies, place it in with the breaded side up, cover with the remaining butter distributed in flakes, and fry in a moderately warm oven for approximately 40 minutes, during which time pour the butter in the pan over it frequently
If desired, the butter can be diluted with 2 decilitres of boiling water
Garnish as previously, serve with lemon or mushroom sauce and boiled potatoes
Alternatively, after the fish piece has been rubbed with lemon juice, cut it across into 1 1/2 cm thick slices, which are beaten with a damp meat mallet
Dip the fish slices in beaten egg, turn in crushed hardtack, fry in butter on the stovetop and serve with lemon sauce, stewed vegetables or potato purée

title: Stekt helgeflundra (Roasted Halibut)
description: Prepared with halibut, vinegar, and rusks.
steps: Clean the fish, rinse it, and scald the dark side with hot water and scrape it.
Rub it with vinegar and let it lie in water with the salt for 1 hour.
Remove the fish and dry it with a cloth, score it on one side and place it in a baking pan greased over as large an area as the fish occupies.
Divide the remaining butter into small flakes and place on top of the fish, sprinkle with crushed rusks and put in a fairly hot oven.
When brown, add boiling water and baste every ten minutes.
Roasting takes ½ to ¾ hour.
When the fish is roasted, place it on a platter.
Strain the sauce and add the lemon juice and taste.
Garnish the fish with parsley and lemon sliced into rounds.
Serve the sauce in a separate sauce bowl.

title: Stekt Kalvbräss med Ärter (Fried Calf Thymus with Peas)
description: Prepared with peas, white pepper, and rusks.
steps: Let the calf thymus soak in water, changing it often, so that all blood is drawn out.
Blanch it for 10 minutes and place in a bowl with fresh water.
When the thymus is cold, clean it well, removing cartilage and membranes, and place it in a cloth under light pressure for about 1 hour.
Cut it into 8 mm thick slices, sprinkle with spices, dip in the egg mixed with water, and turn in the crushed rusks.
Fry the slices a beautiful golden brown in the butter and arrange in a wreath on a round plate.
Empty the peas with a spoon into a saucepan, bring to a boil and place with a slotted spoon in the middle of the plate.
Place the cold butter in flakes over the peas.
Garnish with parsley and serve as a breakfast dish.

title: Stekt kalvfilé (Roasted Veal Fillet)
description: Prepared with veal, lard, and white pepper.
steps: Clean the fillets, dry them with a cloth wrung out in hot water, and lard with fine lard strips in even rows.
Brown the butter in an iron pot, place the fillets in, brown nicely on all sides and sprinkle with a mixture of salt and pepper.
Gradually add the boiling broth and cream and let the fillets roast slowly with the lid tightly closed until tender, or 30-40 minutes, during which time they should be basted often and turned.
Cut them, lay them together again so they retain their form, place on a warm serving platter and garnish with salad or parsley.
Strain the sauce, skim it, heat it and taste it, and if desired add the truffle cut into strips and pour over the meat.
Serve with peas or French potatoes.
If a thinner sauce is desired, it can be thickened with a little butter and flour.
The lard can be omitted and the fillets prepared in the same way otherwise.

title: Stekt kalvfricandeau (Roasted Veal Fricandeau)
description: Prepared with veal, lard, and carrot.

ingredients.name: boneless veal from the inner thigh
ingredients.sourceText: 1 kg boneless veal from the inner thigh

steps: The meat is dried with a cloth wrung out in hot water, pounded with a damp meat mallet, larded with 1 hg of the lard, cut into fine strips dipped in a mixture of salt and pepper, rubbed with the rest of the seasonings and tied so that it gets a nice shape.

The butter is browned in a cooking pot, which should not be larger than to just fit the meat snugly. The meat is placed in it and browned nicely on all sides; when it is half browned, the prepared carrot, cut in slices, the peeled onion and the parsley are added.
When the meat is browned, it is placed on the remaining lard, half of the broth is added and the meat is allowed to cook for 1/2 hour, during which it is basted and turned once.
The rest of the broth is added and the meat is allowed to cook until it is so tender that it can be cut with a fork.

It is carefully taken up, cut with a sharp knife into thin slices, which are laid together so that the roast retains its shape. Placed on a warm platter, garnished with mixed vegetables or vegetable pasties and salad or parsley.
Served with reduced sauce, seasoned with cream and salads.

title: Stekt kalvlever (Fried Calf's Liver)
description: Prepared with liver, lard, and white pepper.
steps: The liver, which should be light and tender, should soak in water for about 0.5 hour, then be well dried, cleaned and larded with fine strips of lard rolled in a mixture of salt and pepper.
Season the liver with the remaining spices and wrap it in the caul (which usually comes with the purchase), which is sewn or fastened together with kitchen twine.
Brown the butter in an iron pot, place the liver in it, brown on all sides and add the milk gradually. Let it cook slowly with the lid tightly closed for about 1.5 hours, basting it frequently.
Remove the caul, slice the liver thinly, place on a warm serving dish, pour a little of the sauce over it and serve the rest of the sauce in a sauce boat.
The sauce is made as in recipe no. 429 and, if desired, mixed with grated mesost cheese.
Serve with boiled potatoes and lingonberry jam.

title: Stekt kalvsadel (Roasted Veal Loin)
description: Prepared with veal, lard, and white pepper.
steps: By saddle is meant the two connected chop rows. The saddle is trimmed and should hang for a couple of days so that the meat becomes tender. The membrane is carefully removed and the saddle is larded in dense rows with fine lard strips, which are rolled in a mixture of salt and pepper.

The butter is browned in a long pan, the saddle is placed in it with the larded side up, put in a warm oven and browned while frequently basted with the butter in the pan. It is sprinkled with the rest of the seasonings, diluted with the boiling broth and allowed to cook until tender, or about 1 1/2 hours, during which it is basted every 10 minutes. If it becomes too brown, cover it with a butter-brushed paper.

The saddle is removed, the meat is loosened neatly on both sides of the backbone, placed on a cutting board and cut across into beautiful slices, which are arranged on the saddle so that it looks whole. It is placed on a warm serving dish and garnished with cooked vegetables such as peas, small fresh beans, cauliflower, asparagus, carrots, as well as French potatoes and green salad or parsley. Served with strained sauce (see no. 429), mixed with thick cream, sherry or Madeira and a little lemon juice.

It is sprinkled with the rest of the seasonings, diluted with the boiling broth and allowed to cook until tender, or about 1 1/2 hours, during which it is basted every 10 minutes. If it becomes too brown, cover it with a butter-brushed paper.

The saddle is removed, the meat is loosened neatly on both sides of the backbone, placed on a cutting board and cut across into beautiful slices, which are arranged on the saddle so that it looks whole. It is placed on a warm serving dish and garnished with cooked vegetables such as peas, small fresh beans, cauliflower, asparagus, carrots, as well as French potatoes and green salad or parsley. Served with strained sauce (see no. 429), mixed with thick cream, sherry or Madeira and a little lemon juice.

title: Stekt Oxfilé Med Legymsalad (Roasted Beef Fillet with Vegetable Salad)
description: A salad made with beef, white pepper, and broth.
steps: The fillet, which should have hung until properly tender, is trimmed (sinews and membranes removed), dried with a cloth wrung in hot water, and tied so it takes a nice form.
Brown the butter in an iron pot not larger than needed to fit the meat, place the fillet in and brown well on all sides, sprinkle with a mixture of salt and pepper.
Place in a hot oven, dilute with the boiling broth and wine, and roast 30–40 minutes, basting frequently.
Remove the roast, cut the string, and slice the fillet into thin slices, which are laid back together so it retains its form, and placed on a 4 cm. high base cut from the wheat bread.
The base should have the same length as the fillet and can, if desired, be browned in aspic or covered with tinfoil.
Around the base garnish with small shells cut from raw cabbage leaves, filled alternately with vegetable salad and browned potatoes.
Serve with meat gravy, strained and skimmed, or with truffle sauce (see no. 433).

title: Stekt Oxhare (Roasted Marinated Hare)
description: Prepared with red wine, vinegar, and berries.
steps: Prepare the hare, which should have hung 4–8 days depending on the season, and lard it (see page 232), and place it in a crock.
Mix all marinade ingredients well, then pour over the meat, which should lie in it 2–3 days and must be turned frequently during this time.

Remove the meat, dry it well, tie it so that it takes a nice form, and roast as in no. 474. First dilute with 2 dcl. of the strained marinade, sprinkle with sugar, cover with the anchovy, and then gradually add the cream.
Serve with browned potatoes and reduced sauce (see no. 429), supplemented with 1 tbsp. chopped capers or 2 tbsp. lingonberry jelly.

title: Stekt Rensadel (Roasted Reindeer Loin)
description: Prepared with alcohol, lard, and broth or water.
steps: Place the meat in drinking alcohol overnight, then remove, rinse well and dry with a cloth.
Remove all sinews carefully, and lard the reindeer loin in tight rows with lard cut into fine strips.
Heat the butter in a roasting pan and brown the roast well; then salt it and add the broth little by little, baste often and turn a couple of times during roasting.
Roasting takes 2-2.5 hours.
Remove the reindeer, cut into thin slices and garnish with vegetables.
Strain and skim the meat juices, and prepare the sauce according to general rules for sauces.

title: Stekt rulad av kalvbog (Rolled Roasted Veal Shoulder)

steps: Wash the shoulder with a cloth dipped in hot water.
Carefully cut out the shoulder blade and also the hip.
Spread the meat out; cut the lard into thin slices and cover the veal with it.
Mix pepper and salt and sprinkle over the lard.
Roll up the meat and tie it very loosely with string.
Brown the butter in a long roasting pan, place the roll in it, and put it in the roasting oven to brown on all sides.
Once it has achieved a nice brown color, add the water.
The roll should roast an additional hour, during which it is basted with its gravy every ten minutes.
Remove the roll and cut it into thin slices and garnish with parsley.
Strain the meat gravy, skim it, and prepare the sauce according to general rules for sauces.

title: Stekt Rådjurslever (Fried Roebuck Liver)
description: Prepared with liver, white pepper, and onions.
steps: The liver should lie in water for a couple of hours so the blood will be drawn out.
Wrap it in cloth, remove the membrane, and cut the liver into thin slices.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper and coat in 2 msk. of the flour.
Brown three msk. of butter in a frying pan, add the liver slices, fry quickly on both sides and place on a warm plate.
Brown the rest of the butter with the onion in the frying pan, mix 1 msk. of flour well with the butter and onion.
Add the broth and let the sauce simmer for 5 minutes, then taste and pour over the liver.
Serve with boiled potatoes.

title: Stekt Skinka (Roasted Ham)
description: Prepared with ham, white pepper, and lard.

ingredients.name: good meat gravy or broth
ingredients.sourceText: 3/4 liter good meat gravy or broth

steps: Dry the ham with a cloth wrung out in hot water, and score the rind 1 cm deep in diagonal squares.
Rub the underside and in the scores with a mixture of the salt and pepper.
Spread the lard slices in a roasting pan, place the ham on top with rind side up, put in a warm oven and let it roast until tender, or about 2 1/2 hours.
When the rind pieces turn a beautiful golden color, harden and loosen, remove them and set aside for garnishing.
When the ham has roasted about 1 1/2 hours, add the boiling meat gravy mixed with the parsley and bay leaf, well tied together, and baste over about every 10 minutes.
Place on a warm serving platter, cut, and arrange the slices so that the ham appears whole, garnish with the rind pieces, salad and parsley as well as fluted, cooked potatoes.
Serve with apple sauce, pickled cucumbers, preserved rowan berries and the like. Strain the gravy, skim, boil down, season with meat extract and spices and serve in a sauce bowl.

title: Stekt Surströmming (Fried Fermented Baltic Herring)
description: Prepared with herrings, beer, and potatoes.

ingredients.name: butter (20 grams) for the pan
ingredients.sourceText: 1 tablespoon butter (20 grams) for the pan

ingredients.name: crushed hardtack for the pan
ingredients.sourceText: 1 tablespoon crushed hardtack for the pan

steps: Clean the herrings, remove the bones, rinse them and let them soak in beer for 2 hours
Wrap them in white paper
Peel the potatoes and cut them into slices; peel the onions and chop them finely
Grease a heat-resistant pan with butter and sprinkle with crushed hardtack
On the bottom of the pan, layer potatoes, then herring, then onion and flakes of butter
Continue layering until you have 5 layers of potatoes and 4 layers of herring
On top, distribute the remaining butter in flakes, then sprinkle the crushed hardtack mixed with the crumbled gingerbread cookies
Fry the herring in a hot oven for approximately 1/2 hour
Serve as a breakfast or supper dish

Note: The potatoes can be omitted and the herring fried in the same manner; it can also be eaten directly from the barrel 'au naturel', in which case the herring is only rinsed and served with raw chopped onion and freshly cooked potatoes

title: Stekt Svinfilé (Fried Pork Fillet)
description: Prepared with pork, white pepper, and broth.
steps: The fillets, weighing 2-4 hg each, are trimmed and dried with a cloth wrung out in hot water
Brown the butter in an iron pot, add the fillets, brown well on all sides and sprinkle with seasoning
Add the boiling broth and cream, and let the meat cook slowly with a tight lid until tender, or about 1/2 hour
Cut the fillets into thin slices, which are placed together on a warm platter so they appear whole
Garnish with Russian peas and browned potatoes or with legumes
Strain the sauce (see recipe 429) and pour it over the meat
Serve with red currant jelly

title: Stekt Tjäder (Roasted Black Grouse)
description: Prepared with grouse, lard, and broth.
steps: If the bird is frozen, thaw it in a warm kitchen, clean it, and let it soak in lukewarm milk overnight.
Dry it well, lard it with fine lard strips, and truss it.
Roast the bird in a pot as you would a hazel grouse, but it requires 2-3 hours of roasting depending on whether it is a hen or a cock.
Cut it, garnish (see page 300), and serve with a reduced sauce (see no. 429), mixed with thick cream and cold butter, and if desired, with 1 tablespoon red currant jelly.

title: Stekt tjäder (Roasted Capercaillie)
description: Prepared with lard, broth or cream, and meat.

ingredients.name: ½-1 liter broth or thin cream
ingredients.sourceText: ½-1 liter broth or thin cream

steps: Pluck the capercaillie (the hen is finest), singe, clean out, rinse well and dry. If it has been frozen, soak it in milk overnight. Lard it with lard cut into fine strips and truss.

Heat the butter in a roasting pan, place the capercaillie in it with the breast up, brown it well and salt it. Roast it on low heat and baste occasionally with broth or thin cream. Roasting takes 2-3 hours.
Strain and skim the meat dripping, and prepare the sauce according to general sauce-making rules.
